summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would authorise additional 2022-23 Commonwealth spending outside ordinary annual government services for decisions made since the October 2022-23 Budget, supplementing existing annual appropriations.
It would provide scheduled funding for intergovernmental assistance, new administered outcomes, assets and liabilities, departmental equity injections and corporate Commonwealth entities.
The appropriations would become available at Royal Assent alongside separate ordinary services and parliamentary funding bills, with no additional advance to the Finance Minister.
changes: Financial assistance to states, territories and local governments would be tied to specified outcomes.
Corporate entity payments would have to serve the purposes of the receiving entities.
Appropriations could be transferred into special accounts serving the same purposes.
The legislation would repeal at the beginning of 1 July 2025.
summary.affected: Commonwealth entities and companies, state and territory governments and local government authorities are affected.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: The government introduced the 2022–23 additional estimates appropriation bills, seeking $5.5 billion in total, with allocations including $1.8 billion for Defence, over $1 billion for Social Services (mostly NDIS), nearly $1 billion for Employment and Workplace Relations (apprenticeship wage subsidy), close to $900 million for Health and Aged Care (vaccines, aged‑care reimbursements, COVID‑19 management), and over $235 million for Foreign Affairs and Trade (passport surge and Osaka World Expo pavilion).

speeches.speaker: Carol Brown
speeches.brief: Documents on proposed expenditure for 2023‑24 and additional expenditure for 2022‑23 were tabled, and a motion was passed to refer them, together with the final budget outcome for 2021‑22 and advances under annual Appropriation Acts, to committees for examination and report.
